title: mine evidence to extend FR_REGIONS for India
scope_note: FR_REGIONS is the FRANCE table (normalize.py:243). India's table is IN_STATES (normalize.py:230), wired via STATE_MAPS at normalize.py:250. Audited IN_STATES, ADDR_CANON_COMMON, ADDR_CANON_FR, NAME_CANON and LEET against the India slice.
headline: IN_STATES needs NO extension - every state present in the data is already a key. The real defect is in ADDR_CANON_COMMON's drop family: 'hno' is deleted but its 7.5x more common sibling 'hn' is not (146,010 occurrences). NEW defect, live-confirmed against the real normalize_address.
most_important_number_meaning: occurrences of the address token 'hn' in addr_tokens[India], which ADDR_CANON_COMMON does not delete although it deletes 'h', 'hno' and 'house'

denominators.derivation: sum of by_country[country].rows / addr_tokens[country] over the six profile files; note France appears only in the three test files

findings.title: 'hn' unhandled while 'hno' is deleted - drop family inconsistent
findings.gloss_confidence: LIKELY ('hn' = house number is the author's own knowledge, not a profile field)
findings.arithmetic: 146010 / 10544085 * 1000 = 13.848 per 1k India rows; 146010 / 19527 = 7.48x more frequent than the handled spelling

live_confirmation.method: imported real _upstream/src/normalize.py with stubbed polars, called normalize_address(addr, 'India')

findings.title: block/blk - neither form is a key in ADDR_CANON_COMMON
findings.key_evidence: Of the address-structure noun families in the India vocabulary, 14 of 15 have BOTH long and short form as keys (street/st, road/rd, avenue/ave, lane/ln, drive/dr, sector/sec, colony/col, nagar/ngr, village/vill, building/bldg, floor/fl, apartment/apt, phase/ph, district/dist, taluk/tq). block/blk is the sole family where NEITHER is present.
findings.fold_direction_confidence: SPECULATIVE (profile cannot show which spelling the other source prefers)

findings.confidence: CONFIRMED (frequency) / LIKELY (that the three are synonyms)

IN_STATES needs no extension
findings.arithmetic: 10 of 37 codes absent, and their full names absent too -> those states do not appear in this dataset

findings.confidence: CONFIRMED context, NOT a defect claim
findings.caveat: The uncovered 70% are proper nouns (street/colony/person/place names) that a structural dictionary should not touch. Not a quality score.

france_impact.summary: None of F1-F4 touch a single French row. France is the only scored country, so the expected score effect of every recommendation here is ZERO.
france_impact.france_effective_canon_definition: normalize.py:320-321 = ADDR_CANON_COMMON minus {st,ste,dr,n,s,e,w}, overlaid with ADDR_CANON_FR

gaps.text: The profile does not record per-component tokens. build_profile.py:126-127 splits on [,;] but updates ONE flat Counter, discarding component identity, while normalize_address:333 tests `if ck in smap` on a WHOLE component. So 'hn' = 146,010 is a TOKEN count; how many are the standalone component 'Hn 12' is NOT measurable. This is why F1's frequency is strong while its match-rate effect is an estimate.
gaps.fix: add a profile field recording the token list of each comma-component

gaps.text: No field records the mapping actually applied, so 'unhandled' claims are established by evaluating the dictionary literal against the profile (sound, indirect) rather than observing pipeline output. I did execute the real normalize_address on 7 constructed India strings to confirm the mechanism, but that is a demonstration, not a corpus measurement.

Semantic glosses are the author's own knowledge, not profile fields: 'hn'=house number, 'soc'/'chs'=co-operative housing society, 'distt'=district, and the Hindi/Urdu words marg/gali/vihar/enclave/mohalla/peth/haveli/wadi/layout/kunj. Marked LIKELY. The F1-F4 defects do not depend on them.

No n-gram or co-occurrence field. Cannot tell whether 'marg' and 'road' ever co-occur in the same address, the condition under which folding marg->rd would merge anything. This is why the Hindi/Urdu vocabulary is NOT in the recommendations.
The 253 '2nd' and 3657 '24hr' occurrences cannot be classified as leet vs legitimate from token bags alone, hence F6 is CONFIRMED as a code fact but only LIKELY as a defect.

build_profile.py prunes hapax tokens (prune(), every 8 chunks, drops count<=1) and keeps only the TOP 4000 per country per file. A token that is rare or falls outside the top 4000 is invisible. ABSENCE of a token from these tables is NOT proof it never occurs; all figures are LOWER BOUNDS.
No file under amazon_ml_2026_research/student_resource/dataset/ was opened. Only the six profile JSONs (575-865 KB, parsed one at a time) and _upstream/src/normalize.py were read.
